::: proof
Because $b''(\theta) > 0$ for every $\theta$,
$b'$ is strictly increasing,
so it has an inverse $\invf{b'}$ on its range.
By @thm-edf-mean-variance:

$$
\ba
\mu &= b'(\theta)
&& \text{(mean of an exponential dispersion family)}
\\ \invf{b'}(\mu) &= \theta
&& \text{(apply } \invf{b'} \text{ to both sides)}
\\ &= g(\mu)
&& \text{(definition of the canonical link)}
\ea
$$
:::

::: notes
The condition $b''(\theta) > 0$ holds for any distribution
whose variance $\phi\, b''(\theta)$ is positive,
that is, any distribution that is not concentrated at a single value.
:::
